To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CHEK2 mutation carrier status increases the risk of cancer, especially for the type of cancer that was present in the mutation carrier's proband; (2) the lifetime risks of breast, prostate and colorectal cancer in carriers of a CHEK 2 mutation are 25, 20 and 10%, respectively, and (3) the lifetime risk for a CHEK2+ relative of a CHEK+ proband is 22% for any cancer
the risks of cancer in relatives of CHEK 2 carriers are dependent on the type of CHEK2 mutations and the site of cancer in the proband.
the risk of breast, prostate and colon cancers was significantly elevated among first-degree relatives of probands carrying a CHEK2 founder mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk of cancer for first-degree relatives of carriers of CHEK2 mutations.
the risk of cancer among first-degree relatives of carriers of the CHEK2 mutation, depending on the type of mutation and the type of cancer in the proband.
the relationship between mutation type and cancer in the first-degree relatives of probands, which has not yet been studied.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a CHEK2*1100delC carrier is at a higher risk of breast cancer than of prostate cancer or colon cancer.
the risk of breast, prostate or colorectal cancer in a CHEK2 carrier is dependent on the mutation type and the site of cancer in the index case.
the risk of developing breast, colon and prostate cancer is higher among first-degree relatives of carriers of CHEK2 mutations than in the general population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a CHEK2 founder mutation carrier is at increased risk of cancer, particularly of the cancer in their proband.
a woman with a CHEK mutation and breast cancer is at a higher risk of breast cancer than a woman with a mutation who has colon cancer.
the risk of any cancer is 22% in first-degree relatives, but this is dependent on the type of mutation and on the cancer site in the proband.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk to a carrier of a particular CHEK2 mutation depends not just on the mutation type, but also on the type of cancer in the proband.
the risk of breast, prostate and colorectal cancer among first-degree relatives of a CHEK 2 carrier depends on whether the proband has breast cancer, prostate cancer or colorectal cancer.
the risk of developing a cancer is higher among relatives of patients carrying a CHEK2*1100delC mutation than among relatives of carriers of other CHEK2 mutations.
